title: `ward run`: status-only HTTPS transport
description: Spec §9.3-9.4. In-process client, HTTPS with verification, no redirects, public-destination-only with DNS results bound to the connection, ambient proxy ignored, bounded timeouts, no automatic retry, status-only output.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T14: the synthetic credential reaches only the mocked approved auth header, never argv, environment, files, output or audit
T15 and T16: redirects are not followed; HTTP, user-info, loopback/private/link-local/metadata, IPv6 variants, DNS rebinding, proxy and TLS-disable attempts are rejected
T17 and T18: credential echoes in any encoding never reach agent-facing output; timeouts and ambiguous mutations report safely without duplicate requests

plan: Re-read spec 9.3-9.4 and ADR 0003 from source; re-measure the private-address rules against the canonical URL form WCLI-9 stores.
Domain: pure destination policy - classify a resolved address as public or not (loopback, private, link-local, multicast, metadata, IPv6 and mapped forms) using maintained parsers.

Adapter: in-process HTTPS client that resolves, validates, then binds the connection to a validated address with hostname verification and SNI retained; no redirects, ambient proxy ignored, bounded timeouts and response bytes, no retry.
Application: `ward run` executes the STORED approved snapshot, never the declaration; status-only result; audit admission before delivery and completion after.
Tests T14-T18 over an injected transport plus a local TLS harness for the binding; credential absent from argv, environment, files, output and audit.
Manifest, docs and security-test matrix; full gate green; independent review; PR.

MEASURED: BUN'S node:https HONOURS AN AMBIENT PROXY, AND tls.connect DOES NOT. This is the whole reason the transport is hand-rolled, so it is recorded with its method. Repro: a net listener on 127.0.0.1, then a request to a host whose `lookup` hook returns a public address. With HTTPS_PROXY set to that listener, node:https connected to the listener while the lookup hook still ran for the destination hostname - so an address-validating hook reported a binding that was not the one used. What failed to defeat it: `proxy: ""`, `proxy: false`, an explicit https.Agent, `agent.createConnection` (never called at all - Bun short-circuits to its fetch layer), and `delete process.env.HTTPS_PROXY` in-process (Bun reads the variables at process start). What does defeat it: NO_PROXY=* set in-process, and - the shape chosen - dialling with tls.connect, which consults nothing but the address it is given. Verified positively: tls.connect to a literal with `servername` set to the hostname reports authorized=true, and Bun refuses an IP passed as servername outright (ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE), so the SNI/IP choice cannot be made silently.

THE FOUR CHECKS OPUM-AGENT ASKED THE REVIEWER TO MAKE ON THE HAND-ROLLED PATH, carried verbatim so the successor does not have to reconstruct them: (1) SNI and hostname verification ACTUALLY ENFORCED - `authorized`, not merely rejectUnauthorized left at its default; (2) no redirect following; (3) the dialled address is the validated one, with no second resolution; (4) a test proving HTTPS_PROXY set in the environment does not change the dial. All four are currently evidenced in test/transport.test.ts, but by this session's own tests, which is not a review. The fourth is the claim-versus-mechanism case and is built with a POSITIVE CONTROL in the same invocation: test/fixtures/transport-proxy-probe.ts runs node:https first (which must reach the parent's listener) and this transport second (which must not), and the assertion is the pair - listener count exactly 1, subject outcome exactly a response. Mutating the subject to use https.request reddens it exactly: the count goes 1 to 2 and the outcome flips - measured, not predicted.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW, THREE ROUNDS, on opum-ai/ward-cli#67. Dispatched per spec 15 as a separate reviewer grounded on this repository's lore review profile, and not by the session that wrote the code.

Round 1 found a CONFIRMED high-severity defect. An approved header value could reach the socket as CR or LF: the domain scanned the value's code points, the transport scanned its UTF-8 bytes, and the request line was written as latin1. U+010A holds no control byte and none in its UTF-8 encoding, but latin1 maps it to its low byte, 0x0A - so a declared value passed both guards and was written as a bare LF, turning one request into two, the second a method and path nobody approved, carrying the credential. Fixed at both ends so that the bytes validated are the bytes written. The regression tests were run against the pre-fix bytes first and required to fail there: pre-fix the crafted value left as two requests, post-fix nothing is sent.

Round 2 confirmed the header defect closed (28 hostile placements, none reachable through the product) and left the credential half of the same class open: the admission re-check covered the approval but not the secret, so a rotation landing in that window delivered the superseded value to the approved endpoint while the vault held the replacement, with neither audit record able to show it. Fixed by comparing the secret id and revision inside the admission transaction. The rotation row flipped to secret_changed, 0 transport calls, no audit records; with the re-check removed the run completes and delivers the stale value, which is the failure the check exists to prevent.

Round 3 verified all three closed and swept all 1,112,064 code points to confirm the new predicate refuses exactly those above U+00FF and accepts nothing it previously refused.

Known gaps, named rather than left silent. The shipped defaultResolve is not measured at the syscall level - no second resolution rests on reading tls.connect with a literal host, not on a measurement. No TLS measurement here uses a real public chain. Whether any runtime reaches the explicit authorized check is unmeasured, and that branch is recorded as a second line rather than the enforcement. The credential-rotation race was modelled in-process against the real store, not by racing two operating-system processes. The credential guarantee is at admission, not at write, which is spec 9.4's admission-time semantics and the same boundary revocation has.

F7, a judgement call, recorded so it can be overruled. profileSnapshotVersion stays 1 although this change narrowed what normalizeProfile accepts, and the rule above the constant says to bump when the accepted set changes. The reason: this change can only refuse more, never accept more, so a snapshot it newly rejects fails closed at parse and no stored record is reinterpreted in either direction. The cost is accepted and named in the comment - such a vault reports vault_state_malformed where vault_format_unsupported would describe a correctly-refused record better. The reviewer confirmed the premise independently by code-point sweep and would not bump. WCLI-38 carries the release-time obligation this reasoning would otherwise have left ungated, pointed at from WCLI-1.

DOCS SLICE. docs/security-tests.md is deliberately NOT created here. WCLI-15 owns that matrix by its own title and description, and its rows for T14-T18 need the tests this task lands, so a partial file written here would be a second owner for one artifact. What WCLI-15 needs is the mapping in this task's final summary. An ADR is owed and was added: ADR 0009 records that the transport departs from spec 9.3's literal wording - use an in-process HTTP client - because Bun 1.3.14's node:https cannot be made to ignore an ambient proxy, and that without the record the obvious repair to a hand-written request line reintroduces the defect. WCLI-15's dependency list omits WCLI-10; noted on WCLI-1 rather than edited here.
finalSummary:
Delivered on opum-ai/ward-cli#67 from branch feat/WCLI-10-status-only-https-transport. CI run ids on the reviewed source head dec1ed3, all three required contexts green on that SHA's own runs and read from the commit's check-runs rather than from an earlier run: Check 109282203449, Docs 109282203770, Tracker integrity 109282203801.

ward run delivers an approved credential to an approved endpoint and reports status only. Destination policy is default-deny over net.BlockList: IPv6 is allow-listed into 2000::/3 and narrowed inside it, IPv4 is judged by the IANA special-purpose registry, and the mapped, NAT64 and 6to4 forms are refused as a class rather than unwrapped. The dial is tls.connect to an address literal that passed that policy, with the hostname kept separately as the SNI name, so there is no second resolution for a rebinding answer to reach. The request is one hand-written HTTP/1.1 line set and the body is never read. Admission and completion are separate transactions, so the vault write lock is never held across network I/O.

An independent reviewer found, and this task fixed, a real injection defect: a declared header value could be written to the socket as CR or LF, splitting one request into two with the credential attached to the second. The suite is 604 tests, up from 599 at the start of the session, and every new case was run against the pre-fix bytes first and required to fail there before being accepted as evidence.

MAPPING FOR WCLI-15 - the rows this task owes docs/security-tests.md, which WCLI-15 owns. T14 Delivery, in test/run.test.ts: "it is in one header and absent from argv, environment, files, output and audit"; "the buffer the run handed the transport is zeroed once it has answered"; "a credential carrying a control byte is refused and nothing is sent". T15 Redirects, in test/transport.test.ts: "a redirect is not followed: the server is contacted once and the status is reported". T16 Network restrictions, in test/transport.test.ts: the refusal table covering loopback, private, link-local metadata, CGNAT, multicast and reserved IPv4 plus the IPv6, IPv4-mapped, NAT64 and 6to4 variants; "an unresolvable name sends nothing"; "the shipped transport refuses loopback by default"; "HTTPS_PROXY reaches node:https and does not reach Ward's transport", which is the proxy claim carried with its positive control in the same invocation; "the name is resolved once, on a path that reaches a server"; and "a header value that would truncate to a line break is refused, and nothing is sent". T17 Response disclosure, in test/transport.test.ts: "a response body echoing the credential never reaches the caller"; "a response that is not a status line is indeterminate, not a number read out of it". T18 Network failure, in test/run.test.ts: "an indeterminate outcome is reported as indeterminate, with exactly one request"; "a non-2xx status is reported as failed with the status, and asked once".

Which of those used mocks: none of T14-T18. Every transport case runs against a real socket and a real TLS server; the only substituted material is the trust anchor, a throwaway CA under test/fixtures/tls that is trusted nowhere and exists so a local server can be reached at all. The resolver is injected so a test can choose what a name answers with, and the address policy then runs on that answer exactly as it does in production.

WCLI-15's dependency list should gain WCLI-10: its T14-T18 rows cannot be written before this task's tests exist. Noted on WCLI-1 rather than edited here.
